checks.reason: Aircraft jumping at EDRF from 2025 is confirmed: a solo jumper left a Cessna at about 3,000 m over the In den Almen field on Saturday 2025-08-30 (police/dpa), and the club's 13–14 June 2026 airfield festival programme lists tandem jumps. All dated jumps fall in June–September and Skyhopping (which names Bad Dürkheim as its recommended site) publishes no dates, so nothing supports 'active' (all-year); Codex inferred it from an absence of weekend restrictions.

checks.reason: This rests on dated evidence that jumping stopped, not on an absence of evidence. The former tandem operator Springwerk states (notice dated 2024-10-20) that it has run no tandems at Breitscheid since 2023-05-01 and will not resume. The club's status page, marked [Update 2026-10], says there are still no sport, training or tandem jumps, citing unresolved hurdles with the municipality; Facebook also says the jump aircraft was lost after a change of owner. The club hopes to restart with no date. An August 2026 gliding-competition briefing repeats a 'Breitscheid Sprungbetrieb' NOTAM line but shows no actual jumps.

sources.what: FSV Breitscheid board notice, [Update 2026-10]: 'noch immer keinen Sprungbetrieb', no tandems, no courses, restart at an unspecified later time.
Springwerk notice dated 2024-10-20: no tandem jumps at Breitscheid since 2023-05-01; business will not resume.

checks.reason: The LuBB decision of 2025-02-18 revokes the EDUS operating approval, takes the land out of aviation planning, and orders closure markings. It records that the sole user, Aircraft Maintenance & Consulting GmbH (the dropzone operator named in DFV), agreed to the closure and returned its Part 145 approval on 2024-12-02. The new owner is a solar company with no aviation purpose, and 2025 municipal plans for a solar park on 'Flugplatz Schacksdorf' corroborate this.

sources.what: Official revocation of the EDUS approval dated 2025-02-18 (read in full); operation allowed at most until 2025-04-30 to remove aircraft.
Municipal 2025 land-use change for the 'Solarpark Finsterwalde/Schacksdorf - Flugplatz Schacksdorf'.
rbb 2025-12-05: solar park and battery storage planned on the former airfield.

checks.reason: Haller Tagblatt/SWP of 2023-05-04 report that the local motor-flying club won an eviction action and the Para-Club is leaving Weckrieden. The club's own pages say it currently cannot practise its sport and is looking for a landing meadow. The second listed operator, Blue Sky Adventures (same contact as the Para Club), now takes off from Würth Airport (EDTY) and lands near Brachbach, Untermünkheim (OSM 49.1847, 9.7242, about 8 km from Weckrieden), and advertises 2026 tandem dates 'in Schwäbisch Hall'. That operation is a lead for a separate record; it is not jumping at Weckrieden.
